title: Buddy Petit joins Humphrey's band from Mandeville
summary: Humphrey recalls Petit leaving Mandeville to join his band with Lee Collins for about two months around 1926, and names the personnel.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: All right, now, we're talking to Earl Humphrey. Today is November 30th, 1968. Now, could you tell us about when you were playing with Buddy Petit? What is all you can remember about Buddy Petit?

Well, I suppose it must have been just about 1926. And we had a gig over in Mandeville every other Saturday night. In the hotel. Buddy was stationed over there with another man. And it looks as though he had gotten tired of being over there, kind of lonesome, just working on weekends. So he decided to come home and join us in the Orleans with Lee Collins and Earl Humphrey's band. That was our band. So you mean you had two companies? We only had one until Buddy joined us. So Buddy, he got on the train. We wasn't expecting to come over with us. Anyhow, when we looked around, the train had gone. Buddy had slipped on the train. Anyhow, come on over. Now, naturally, we had a little work. And he stayed with us for about two months. And then he decided to go back to Mandeville. But during the time he was with us, we did pretty well.
Tell me, what's George Lewis in that band?
George Lewis was in that band. George Lewis was in that band.
George, can you tell, who else was in the band? Yeah. Yeah.

Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. and little dad, Vincent, Turner Banja, Roy Evans on drums, Earl Hunter, myself on trombone, Lee Collins on trumpet, and with the addition of Buddy, maybe we had two trumpets for us. Yes.
